From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP and evaluation gates for Mediflow pilot

Hi Ellen — really glad the demo landed. I attached a draft MAP and a starter test-case CSV that maps each acceptance test to an owner and pass/fail metric. High-level summary below — full details in mediflow_map_v1.xlsx and eval_test_cases.csv.

Proposed pilot: 6-week evaluation (2 week integration, 3 week operational run, 1 week review + close). Goal: produce a production decision (pilot accepted or decommission) by end of week 6.

Success criteria (must all be met unless otherwise noted):
- Functional: NER F1 >= 0.86 on your annotated validation set (see test-case row IDs TC-01..TC-06).
- Performance: 95th percentile latency <= 220ms at 100 QPS, 99th <= 420ms during synthetic load spike.
- Reliability: sustained availability >= 99.5% during operational run window (excl. scheduled maintenance).
- Cost: token cost per transaction within 15% of the estimate in our quote (we'll post actual unit costs in week 4).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 summary provided; KMS integration tested for at-rest keys; audit logs flowing to your SIEM during integration.

Exit gates (go/no-go triggers):
- Go if: all functional tests pass and the performance & reliability thresholds are met for the 3-week operational run.
- Partial go / conditional go: if functional tests pass but 95/99latency exceed thresholds, we run an optimization sprint (two weeks) with quantization/batching config — acceptance if improvements hit 95/99 targets or if there is a mutually agreed SLA extension.
- No-go: critical security gaps (KMS/audit failures) or F1 below 0.80 after remediation.

Acceptance tests (owner in parens):
- TC-01..TC-06: core NER labeled set (Mediflow eng) — pass if F1 >= 0.86.
- TC-07: end-to-end integration (Redwood SRE + Mediflow eng) — pass if requests succeed and logs appear in SIEM.
- TC-08: load ramp and failover (Redwood infra) — pass if availability > 99.5% and no data loss.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to schedule the integration kickoff (availability windows in the attached MAP).
2) Mediflow to share the annotated NER set and a representative traffic profile (Raj).
3) Redwood to provision a dedicated trial pool and share initial runbook.

Attachments: mediflow_map_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), eval_test_cases.csv (test matrix), SOC2_summary.pdf (security snapshot).

Would 2027-10-05 at 10am PT for the kickoff work?

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
